## Summary
DELETE is a hard delete that cascades to observations. A soft delete needs a separate `deleted_at` state, filtering on every query, and a decision on MRN reuse.

## Findings
| id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARC-001 | high | data | sample-app/src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__init.sql:26 | `ON DELETE CASCADE`: deleting a patient physically removes their observations today | Replace the delete with `deleted_at` (timestamp); keep the FK, which then never fires. |
| ARC-002 | medium | correctness | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/repository/PatientRepository.java:12 | Every finder must exclude deleted rows, and `uq_patient_mrn` still counts deleted rows, so an MRN cannot be registered again | `@SQLRestriction("deleted_at is null")` on Patient; decide whether MRN reuse is allowed. |
| ARC-003 | medium | domain | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/domain/Patient.java:43 | `active` is an administrative flag in FHIR; deleted and inactive are distinct states | Do not overload `active`; add `deleted_at`. |
| ARC-004 | low | compliance | context/domain/fhir-lite-glossary.md:22 | Glossary rule 5 already calls delete a soft concern in real systems | Agree the retention period with Legal and record it in an ADR. |

- DELETE keeps its ADMIN-only rule and returns 204; the row is marked deleted.
